title: Domain and Range
seo_title: Algebra I Domain and Range Worksheets (TEKS A.2A)
standard_text: A.2A determine the domain and range of a linear function in mathematical problems; determine reasonable domain and range values for real-world situations, both continuous and discrete; and represent domain and range using inequalities; A.6A determine the domain and range of quadratic functions and represent the domain and range using inequalities; A.9A determine the domain and range of exponential functions of the form f(x) = ab^x and represent the domain and range using inequalities
meta_desc: Free Algebra I domain and range worksheets for Texas TEKS A.2A, A.6A and A.9A: ordered pairs, graphs, linear, quadratic and exponential rules, inequality notation and reasonable values in context. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Domain: the x-values. Range: the y-values.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The domain is all the inputs (x-values). The range is all the outputs (y-values).
  • A linear function like f(x) = 2x + 1 has all real numbers for both.
  • A quadratic opening up has range y ≥ the y-value of the vertex.
  • An exponential function f(x) = abx with a > 0 has range y > 0.
  • In real situations, keep only values that make sense: no negative time, whole numbers for people.

Examples

Example

f(x) = (x − 2)2 + 3

vertex (2, 3), opens up

Answer: domain: all real numbers; range: y ≥ 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping domain and rangeDomain is x; range is y.
Using ( ) for an included endpointUse [ ] when the endpoint is included.
Allowing impossible values in contextTime and counts cannot be negative.

items.q: What is the domain of the relation {(−3, 1), (−2, 1), (−4, 2), (3, −1), (5, −4)}?
items.e: The domain is the set of inputs (the x-values): {−4, −3, −2, 3, 5}.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = (x − 2)2 + 1?
items.e: The vertex is (2, 1). The parabola opens up, so the smallest value of y is 1: y ≥ 1. The domain is all real numbers.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = (x + 2)2 + 8?
items.e: The vertex is (−2, 8). The parabola opens up, so the smallest value of y is 8: y ≥ 8. The domain is all real numbers.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = (x + 2)2 − 4?
items.e: The vertex is (−2, −4). The parabola opens up, so the smallest value of y is −4: y ≥ −4. The domain is all real numbers.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −(x + 4)2 − 4?
items.e: The vertex is (−4, −4). The parabola opens down, so the largest value of y is −4: y ≤ −4. The domain is all real numbers.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 4x + 5?
items.e: A non-horizontal line goes up and down forever, so the range is all real numbers.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = (x − 5)2 + 2?
items.e: The vertex is (5, 2). The parabola opens up, so the smallest value of y is 2: y ≥ 2. The domain is all real numbers.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = −(x + 3)2 + 7?
items.e: The vertex is (−3, 7). The parabola opens down, so the largest value of y is 7: y ≤ 7. The domain is all real numbers.

items.q: What is the range of g(x) = |x − 1| + 3?
items.e: An absolute value is never negative, so the smallest value of |x − 1| + 3 is 3. So y ≥ 3.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = (x + 1)2 + 6?
items.e: The vertex is (−1, 6). The parabola opens up, so the smallest value of y is 6: y ≥ 6. The domain is all real numbers.

items.q: What is the domain of h(x) = √(x + 1) − 4?

items.q: Which inequality means the same as (−8, 0]?
items.e: [ means included (≤), ( means not included (<): −8 < x ≤ 0.

items.e: The values go up forever, and ∞ always gets a parenthesis: [4, ∞).

items.q: Write −4 ≤ x < −1 in interval notation.
items.e: Use a square bracket [ ] when the endpoint is included (≤) and a parenthesis ( ) when it is not (<): [−4, −1).

What is the domain of f(x) = x2 − 3?
items.e: You can square any number: all real numbers. (The range is y ≥ −3.)

items.q: A store sells boxes of 12 donuts. D(b) = 12b is the number of donuts in b boxes. Which number cannot be in the range?
items.e: Outputs are multiples of 12. 30 is not.

items.q: Which situation has a domain of whole numbers only?
c: The distance a car travels in t hours
The weight of p pounds of apples
items.e: You can't buy part of a pencil: the cost of buying n pencils.

items.q: A(w) = w(20 − w) is the area of a rectangle with perimeter 40 cm and width w. What is a reasonable domain?
items.e: Both the width and the length 20 − w must be positive: 0 < w < 20.

items.q: A car's 15-gallon tank is full. It uses 1 gallon every 30 miles. G(d) is the fuel left after d miles. What is a reasonable domain?
items.e: The tank lasts 15 × 30 = 450 miles: 0 ≤ d ≤ 450.

items.q: The range of f(x) = −x2 + 9 is…
items.e: It opens down with vertex (0, 9), so the largest value is 9: y ≤ 9.

items.q: What are the domain and range of f(x) = 7 (a horizontal line)?
items.e: Every input is allowed, but the only output is 7: domain all real numbers, range {7}.

items.q: A ball is dropped from a 64 ft tower and lands after 2 seconds. h(t) is its height in feet. What is the range?
items.e: The height goes from 64 ft down to 0 ft: 0 ≤ h ≤ 64.

items.q: Which interval is the domain of a function that is defined for every number greater than −3?
items.e: Greater than −3, not including −3: (−3, ∞).

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = x − 1?
items.e: A non-horizontal line goes up and down forever, so the range is all real numbers.
